title: Choose a modern utility direction
question: These three keep the familiar utility structure while giving Clickity a more specific modern identity.

options.label: Control Deck
options.lineage: compact audio mixers and streaming control decks
options.thesis: Timing, repeat, and targeting become three precise control channels feeding one unmistakable run control.
options.viewport: A slim status header leads into three stacked control channels, each with a large value and compact toggles, while a mint start strip spans the bottom edge.
options.risk: Its precision feels modern and useful, but too many track-like controls could make Clickity resemble streaming software.

options.label: Quick Panel
options.thesis: The most-used choices sit in one thumb-readable command surface, with advanced coordinates appearing only when relevant.
options.viewport: A large ready-state and start control occupy the top third, followed by broad timing and mouse-button rows, with target details expanding below on demand.
options.risk: Its speed and gaming familiarity are excellent, but progressive disclosure must not hide settings power users expect.

options.label: Peripheral Studio
options.thesis: A simplified mouse diagram and disciplined settings rail make click behavior feel tangible without resorting to RGB theatrics.
options.viewport: A compact mouse diagram and live status share the top region, with timing and repeat controls below in a clean two-column rail and a violet start action at the base.
options.risk: It fits the gaming audience naturally, but may imply Clickity is companion software for a specific mouse.

canonCard.label: Modern Utility Panel
canonCard.thesis: The familiar card-based settings panel from the first round, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A compact header and status pill lead into timing, click, and target cards, ending with a full-width blue start button.
canonCard.risk: It is the easiest to understand and the hardest to remember.
